executiveSummary: GM0402's 2025 identity, boundary, population, 43 neighbourhoods, one BAG place, three settlements and Gooi en Vechtstreek membership are coherent; all ten canonical presets also pass the six-checkpoint/eight-service deterministic gate. Release is nevertheless correction-required. Hilversum's official assessment describes external sea/river flooding as insignificant-to-small and spatially limited mainly to Kerkelanden, the southwest and shallow effects in Hilversumse Meent, while local cloudburst pooling follows sharp terrain differences and identified sewer/road low points. The model instead holds 0.572962 normalized river inundation stress through T+72, reaches 13,544 affected people-equivalent and reuses exactly the same 43-neighbourhood order for storm, pluvial, river, coastal wind, heat, winter, cyber and wildfire. A controlled source in verified mixed woodland in Landelijk Gebied 94 produces direct fire 0.622322 and smoke 0.621963, yet that containing neighbourhood ranks 40th while Trompenberg-Zuid ranks first. Media Park is an official regional risk-focus area for cascading accident, power, extreme-weather and malicious-threat effects, but ranks only 24th under untargeted cyber. Twelve NWB logical links, four station points and 144 scheduled stops do not establish event-time A1/A27/ring/rail/tunnel access, and registered Tergooi MC offer is not live acceptance or backup. Public water assets, Liander/planning, antenna, education and preparedness records are useful dated context but not connected topology, outage, occupancy, stock or restoration. Retain official geography, narrow hazard eligibility and deterministic arithmetic; suppress exact local consequence, access, outage and recovery claims unless publisher, version, issue/valid time, coverage, licence, evidence class and Unknown/NoData semantics are explicit.

evidenceSources.publisher: Centraal Bureau voor de Statistiek / PDOK / Kadaster
evidenceSources.title: GM0402 official 2025 municipality, neighbourhood, place and settlement geography and statistics
evidenceSources.edition: CBS Wijken en buurten 2025; CBS/PDOK inputs retrieved 31 August 2026; BRT settlement snapshot retrieved 31 August 2026
supports: The annual CC BY 4.0 CBS/PDOK input identifies GM0402 as Hilversum and reports 94,393 residents, density 2,070/km², 18.9% aged 65 or older and 19,184 one-person households; the generated centre lies inside the 2025 boundary.

All 43 published neighbourhood rows sum to 94,405 residents, twelve above the municipality row (+0.013%); households sum to 44,865 and rounded age-65-plus rows to 17,875. Deterministic allocation reconciles to the official total without rewriting source rows.
One active BAG woonplaats is Hilversum. BRT contributes Hilversum and Hilversumse Meent as woonkernen and Egelshoek as a buurtschap; labels do not carry fabricated population or operational roles.

CBS registered residents and annual attributes are administrative context, not event-time occupants, patients, workers, visitors or responders. BAG/PDOK place data carries Public Domain Mark 1.0; suppressed, null and not-applicable fields remain NoData rather than zero.

evidenceSources.title: Gemeentelijk Watermanagementplan Hilversum 2021-2026
evidenceSources.edition: Plan dated 14 April 2020, adopted 9 September 2020 for 2021-2026
supports: The plan inventories 488 km of pipe: 205 km foul-water, 204 km stormwater, 6 km infiltration sewer, 62 km combined and 11 km force main, plus 13,410 inspection chambers, 91 stormwater outlets, sixty pumps and one external combined-sewer overflow.

Wastewater from western Hilversum goes to RWZI Horstermeer, eastern wastewater to RWZI Hilversum at Anna's Hoeve, while Hilversumse Meent foul water enters Bussum's sewer system. That is real cross-boundary service geography absent from a municipal scalar.

The municipality accepts temporary stormwater on streets and, pending measures, some wastewater-on-street and building risk. It uses 30 mm in one hour as a storm-sewer design case and 70 mm in one hour as a public-space building-damage design case, not as guaranteed event performance.

The plan maps distinct water-overload areas and names Loswal, Laapersveld, Utrechtseweg, Oude Haven and Over het Spoor measures. Its documentary inventory has no standard reuse licence, live blockage/pump/control state, catchment API, event rainfall or restoration cadence.

evidenceSources.title: Definitive PlanMER for the Hilversum 2040 environmental vision
evidenceSources.edition: Definitive report dated 12 December 2022; source climate maps largely 2021-2022
supports: The municipal assessment calls external sea/river flood probability insignificant-to-small. It identifies incomplete/limited mapped depth mainly for Kerkelanden and the southwest, a very small place-based probability now and in 2050, and limited shallow 20-50 cm damage in Hilversumse Meent.

It separately identifies recurrent pluvial problems in Hilversumse Meent, the centre mixed sewer, Lorentzweg/Kleine Drift, Havenkwartier, Laapersveld, Kerkelanden and the southwest; parts encounter problems around 40 mm because steep local terrain routes water to low points.

The west is substantially lower than the centre/east and approaches below NAP toward the Loosdrechtse Plassen, with peat replacing sandy soils. Urban infiltration opportunity is mostly very high but lower in Hilversumse Meent. These gradients contradict municipality-wide uniform flood stress.

The report rates nature-fire sensitivity average-to-high around Goois Natuurreservaat, Spanderswoud, Westerheide, Zuiderheide and Hilversum airfield, depending on drought, vegetation, visitors and weather. Planning maps and narrative establish mechanism and scope, not a current incident, exact cell severity or operational licence/cadence.

evidenceSources.publisher: Waterschap Amstel, Gooi en Vecht / Het Waterschapshuis
evidenceSources.title: Hilversum urban-water responsibilities, completed A27 storage and public IMWA/DAMO assets
evidenceSources.edition: AGV responsibility transfer effective 1 January 2024; A27 storage opened February 2025; HWH snapshot retrieved 3 September 2026
supports: AGV took over management and maintenance of Hilversum's urban surface water on 1 January 2024 and is still developing a water-area plan for operating levels, system function and measures. The current page is programme context, not an already selected operating rule set.

AGV reports that a 35-hectare nature/recreation and rainwater-storage area near A27 was completed by February 2025; it receives temporary rainwater in dry forest and wet heath. Completed storage does not prove capacity available for every modeled event.

The partial national CC BY-SA 4.0 HWH aggregation assigns 34 points to GM0402: thirteen surface-water pumps, twenty weirs and RWZI Hilversum. Only one asset has non-null capacity, and the public subset omits the municipality's sixty-pump inventory and connected catchments.

No Waterinfo observation or forecast point is assigned inside GM0402 in the deployment snapshot. Contributor/query gaps are NoData, not zero water or safe operation; assets do not establish flow direction, compatible capacity, control, blockage, power/backup, drinking-water pressure/quality or T+72 restoration.

evidenceSources.title: Regionaal Risicoprofiel Gooi en Vechtstreek 2024
evidenceSources.edition: Definitive 2024 risk profile, policy basis for 2025-2028
supports: The four-year regional profile lists storm/wind/rain, cold, heat, flood, nature fire, loss of speech/data, electricity loss, cyberattack and transport incidents as priority risks; regional eligibility is not a Hilversum event probability or magnitude.

It identifies forests/heath and recreation, hospitals and less-self-reliant facilities, studios and visitor venues, intensive road/rail movement, pipelines and high-voltage infrastructure, and says vital-service effects cross regional boundaries.

Media Park in Hilversum is the region's specific risk-focus area because people, economic importance and complexity combine; its stacked scenarios include accidents, electricity loss, extreme weather and malicious threats.

The strategic PDF has no standard machine incident/resource endpoint or stated reuse licence/cadence. It validates preparedness scope, never target compromise, event-time occupancy, dispatch, staffing, stock, backup or restoration.

evidenceSources.title: De Zuid forest-heath recreation context and TOP10NL controlled-source eligibility
evidenceSources.edition: Current GNR area page and 2026 municipal fire guidance; TOP10NL source actuality 2006, registered 24 November 2008
supports: GNR describes De Zuid in Hilversum as 204 ha of forest, heath, pools and old sand-extraction terrain used for walking, cycling, riding and dog recreation. Hilversum's current page warns that dry/warm periods increase nature-fire risk and records a 2026 seasonal smoking ban on Hilversumse Heide.

The controlled point [5.18152,52.19124] lies in CBS Landelijk Gebied 94; a narrow TOP10NL query returns mixed-forest polygons including feature 99380e75-b69c-547d-8997-a7b165bf52c0. This is transparent eligibility, not current fuel or an observed ignition.

TOP10NL is generally CC BY 4.0 and machine-readable, but these source features are old. They cannot supply current moisture, visitor count, ignition/perimeter, spread, smoke, access, firewater, crews or suppression.

evidenceSources.publisher: Rijkswaterstaat / ProRail / OVapi / NDW / Gemeente Hilversum
evidenceSources.title: NWB road skeleton, ProRail stations and Hilversum mobility/access context
evidenceSources.edition: Municipal environmental baseline updated 2021; NWB-Light 1 August 2026; ProRail current registers; GTFS version 9543; snapshots retrieved 2-3 September 2026
supports: The municipality describes a double urban ring with radial roads; external access is oriented to A1, A27 and N201 toward A2. It identifies N525 to A1, A27 junction 33, freight height constraints at tunnels/viaducts, three urban rail hubs and pressure on Media Park, Laapersveld and centre access.

Monthly CC0 NWB creates twelve logical boundary links across A1, A27, N201, N236, N415, N417, N524 and N527. A1, A27 and three N236 edges are repeated physical-corridor series and their 260/150 scenario-unit ceilings are never additive traffic or evacuation capacity.

ProRail geometry places Hilversum, Hilversum Media Park, Hilversum Sportpark and Hollandsche Rading station points inside the full boundary; GTFS version 9543 supplies 144 stop areas. Schedule/point presence is not event-time trains, buses, people, accessibility or throughput.

Zero covered NDW current situations is no matching record at retrieval, not proof that A1/A27, the urban rings, tunnels, viaducts, rail crossings, stations, Tergooi access or supply routes are open. ProRail's July 2026 Sportpark page describes future crossing changes, not present emergency capacity.

evidenceSources.publisher: RIVM / Tergooi MC / Gemeente Hilversum / Liander / Netbeheer Nederland / RDI / DUO
evidenceSources.title: Acute-care, utility, communications, education and first-72-hour preparedness context
evidenceSources.edition: Municipal preparedness programme and May 2026 pilot; RIVM questionnaire v1.1 published 3 July 2026; deployment snapshots retrieved 2-3 September 2026
supports: RIVM CC0 v1.1 locates Tergooi MC at Laan van Tergooi 2 with a reported 24/7 ED, acute obstetrics, seventeen treatment rooms and 26,161 visits in 2025; Tergooi currently confirms 24-hour ED access. Dated offer is not live occupancy, staff, diversion, supplies, backup or acceptance.

One postcode sample identifies Liander substation area OS HILVERSUM JONKERWEG 10-1i and quarterly/monthly large-user planning values. The product is open data but no exact dataset licence identifier was found; one sample is not complete topology, current load, switching, outage, reserve or restoration.

Public snapshots assign 172 RDI antenna-installation sites and 95 DUO education-use records to GM0402. RDI's statutory WFS states no reuse-licence version/fixed cadence; DUO is daily CC BY with version unspecified. Sites do not establish broadcast/mobile coverage, backhaul/power, occupants, shelter designation, accessibility, supplies or operation.

Hilversum's programme says emergency support points are still being developed and tested: a De Geus pilot ran in May 2026, locations/functions were expected to be clarified around end-2026/start-2027, and the municipality says at least one point per 5,000 residents is needed. Plans, guidance and a pilot are not activated sites, trained staffing, radios, generators, water, medicine cooling, stock or 72-hour availability.
